top.title: Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market
top.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira appreciated by N10 against the dollar in the parallel market on Friday, exchanging at N1,445 per dollar, compared with N1,455 on Thursday. Similarly, the naira strengthened in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), appreciating to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market improved by N2 to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official market exchange rates narrowed to N69 per dollar from N77 recorded on Thursday. Meanwhile, the value of interbank turnover in the NFEM fell by 54.5 per cent to $106.9 million from $235.04 million recorded on Thursday. top.title: Cody Campbell once again makes it about himself
top.description: Credit: Keith Inglis on X If there’s anybody who perfectly encapsulates the “get in there and make it about you” meme, it’s Texas Tech booster and oil tycoon Cody Campbell. Campbell has taken on outsized influence in not just investing millions in the Red Raiders athletic program to bring their teams to prominence, but throughout all of college football as well. He has been vocal in advocating for sweeping, transformational changes to the sport, particularly around the Protect College Sports Act and nationalizing television rights . But he has also rubbed others the wrong way with how he handles his business. He publicly clashed with former Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark with complaints over Friday night scheduling. And he’s shown himself to be a bit overly sensitive as he threatened a Lubbock radio station with pulling players from interviews over a critical tweet from a producer. He also regularly positions himself as part of the program through his appearances and messaging, acting as more of an owner or general manager than booster. So when Texas Tech clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance with a victory over TCU on Friday night, it was no surprise that Cody Campbell found a way to elbow himself into the spotlight. The booster showed up at the postgame press conference to ask a question to head coach Joey McGuire about the team having the momentum of a runaway freight train and why he’s so popular. Full exchange between Texas Tech mega-booster Cody Campbell and head coach Joey McGuire as he sat in on the postgame press conference following a win over TCU. Campbell’s question: “So, with all the adversity we dealt with over the last year, everything we’ve been through, can you talk about and I because I’ve seen it, the love that you have for your players, the love they have for you and and for each other, and how that’s gotten us through everything we’ve dealt with and why we’re in the place we’re in once again this year?” — Keith Inglis (@KeithInglisDT) November 27, 2026 Naturally, Cody Campbell will say that he’s only doing this because he wants McGuire and the team to get the respect and love that they are due and it’s all about lifting them up. But in reality, he’s only taking the attention for himself once again. There is no reason for him to be showing up and asking questions at a postgame press conference. None. But because he is the one that’s paying for all of this, he can do whatever he wants. If Campbell really wanted McGuire and the team to get some shine, the best thing he could do is get out of the way and let them actually have the moment for themselves. But that’s something that he seems incapable of understanding. The post Cody Campbell steals the spotlight in crashing Texas Tech press conference appeared first on Awful Announcing .

top.title: Jackson Koivun Wins The 2026 Skins Game
top.description: HOBE SOUND, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 27: Jackson Koivun of the United States plays his shot from the seventh tee during the Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club on November 27, 2026 in Hobe Sound, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) Getty Images Last year saw the return of the popular golf event call the Skins Game. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The 2026 event had the following golfers competing for big-time money. 2026 Skins Game Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun The event, which took place at The Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida, returned to its original format of the event. The competition, which started back in 1983, abandoned the “reverse purse” from 2025, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Unlike 2025, where Xander Schauffele failed to win even a single skin during the event, this event was competitive till the very end. This year there was a serious carryover down the stretch which resulted in an 18th hold worth $2 million dollars. No one could win the hole out-right, which meant they headed to a “19th” hole. The tee box was placed 118 yards from the pin on the 18th hole, and every player got a shot. Closest to the hole, while hitting the green, won the $2 million dollars. Thomas was up first, and missed the green long. Second was Clark, and he too missed the green, landing on the fringe. Koepka was third to hit, and he hit a safe shot in the middle of the green. The pressure was on the 21-year-old Koivun to put his shot inside Koepka, and the result was extremely close to Koepka. The result required an official measurement, which showed Koivun won the hole, and the event. The shot equated in Koivun winning $2.375-million, a total which topped his career earnings so far on the PGA Tour. When all was said and done, the money totals were as follows for the event: Jackson Koivun: $2.375 Million Brooks Koepka: $700,000 Justin Thomas: $475,000 Wyndham Clark: $400,000 The event was much more competitive than the 2025 iteration, and should be deemed as a success. top.title: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often?
top.description: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often? I am not a football manager or a football expert, and I don’t try to be, but I like to think I know a bit about football, having played the game myself for a number of years alongside being a huge football fan, watching many leagues and teams over the years, but most of all, of course, being a passionate Arsenal fan. Now, this may be controversial, but everyone is allowed an opinion, and I like to think, well, I hope, I know what I’m talking about sometimes. But what I would like to see is Mikel Arteta take the risk and sometimes play with two strikers up front. The rest of the formation and the way he decides to set up his team would not be a problem, but I’d genuinely like to see two up front. Why Not Play Havertz and Gyökeres Together? Now, I say this because, as we know, he seems to pick between either Kai Havertz or Viktor Gyökeres, and he rarely goes for the two of them together. But why not? If you haven’t tried it regularly, how do you know if it will work? Now, I don’t mean try it once and if it doesn’t work, give up. I mean give the two a chance to play together on a number of occasions! Everyone has their moans and groans when our strikers are not scoring, and yes, sometimes the delivery is not what it should be, but sometimes you have to take the game into your own hands and try, as we saw with Gyökeres’ goal against Borussia Dortmund the other night, which was a rather sweet strike. So why does Gyökeres seem to score left, right and centre for Sweden but struggle for Arsenal? There may be a number of reasons, but one reason I believe is because he is high in confidence, and more often than not, he is not playing as a lone striker as he tends to do for Arsenal. Sweden seems to have built their team around Gyökeres, and in the Nations League this year he has often played in a strike partnership, notably alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak, hence the great goalscoring form for his country. He scored six goals in five Nations League games this campaign and recently made history by scoring in eight consecutive matches in the competition , across two editions, scoring 12 goals during that run. Gyökeres is a player who can hold the ball up well and make that pass, whereas Havertz tends to struggle in that department depending on who is defending him. But he can offer good off-the-ball movement and good link-up play to the team. So why can the two not play together? (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) Could a Strike Partnership Bring More Goals? top.title: Section 1 moving forward with plan to separate non-public schools during playoffs, despite state objections
top.description: Section 1 is moving forward with a plan that would separate its public and non-public schools during postseason athletic competition, despite the move previously being overturned by a NYSPHSAA appeals panel. (Jim Franco/Times Union) When the Christian Brothers Academy football team takes the field Saturday night at Middletown High School for a Class AA state semifinal against Section 1's Mamaroneck, the Brothers will be doing so against a team from a section that is attempting to separate its public and non-public schools during postseason competition. A win Saturday in Middletown could also put CBA on a collision course for a state championship matchup next week against Syracuse's Christian Brothers Academy. If both CBA teams win their state semifinals this weekend, it would mark the second time in three years that the state title in New York's largest classification is contested between the two private schools that share the same name. First up for the Albany CBA squad is its matchup against Mamaroneck on Saturday at 6 p.m. The Tigers represent Section 1, which recently announced that despite objections from the New York State Public High School Athletic Association, it was moving forward with a planned change to its constitution that would separate private, parochial and charter schools from public schools during postseason athletic competition. That move would leave the non-public schools ineligible to participate in state playoffs. Section 1 announced the change to its constitution in June, following a 69-4 vote of member schools in the section, which includes Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Dutchess counties. Section 1's four non-public members - Albertus Magnus in Nanuet, Ursuline School in New Rochelle, Keio Academy in Purchase and The Lefell School in Hartsdale - were the only four institutions in the section to vote against the amendment. Three of the affected non-public schools filed an appeal with NYSPHSAA, and in July a three-person appeals panel from the state association ruled to overturn that amendment. However, at its October meeting, Section 1 announced plans to move forward with its plan beginning in the 2027-28 school year. In a statement to the Times Union, a Section 1 spokesperson said: "In June, 69 of the 73 schools that cast ballots supported proceeding with the changes, exceeding the two-thirds approval required for passage. Section One's decision to move forward with amendments to its constitution and bylaws is a matter of internal governance and reflects the direction of its member schools." The issue of private, parochial and charter schools - dubbed "schools without boundaries" by NYSPHSAA - competing against public institutions in state championship events has been a hot-button topic in recent years. NYSPHSAA convened an ad hoc committee to address the issue in 2024, which ultimately adopted a plan to provide statewide standards for reclassifying non-public and charter schools based on performance. top.title: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’
top.description: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’ Real Madrid will look to extend their winning run to 11 games in all competitions as they take on Deportivo Alaves this weekend. Heading into the clash, Alaves midfielder Antonio Blanco addressed the media as he offered his thoughts on facing Real Madrid and what it means to him as a player. Blanco came through the ranks at Real Madrid, even making his first-team debut, with Los Blancos still holding 50% of his transfer rights as part of his €4 million move to Alaves in 2023. Blanco wary of Bellingham threat First and foremost, Blanco was asked about the prospect of facing an in-form Jude Bellingham, who has found his best form under the leadership of Jose Mourinho. Blanco has immense respect for Jude Bellingham. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “We know he’s a great player, but we’ll try to stop him. Madrid have many top-level footballers. We have to focus on doing our job to get a good result,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). Blanco, who has rediscovered his best form after a difficult patch, is relishing a packed schedule that sees Alaves play three games in seven days across LaLiga and the Copa del Rey. “What we like is to play matches and if it’s for three days, then all the better. You’re constantly with the tension of competition. Besides, the Copa del Rey is also coming up, a very nice competition that we enjoy playing,” he explained. Confidence heading to the Bernabeu Deportivo Alaves will have a tough challenge on their hands. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Deportivo Alaves will face an intense challenge against an in-form Real Madrid squad. But Blanco believes his team can cause an upset. “We go with confidence after breaking a run where we were struggling. The other day against Deportivo we got the three points and recovered our DNA. We’ll see how tomorrow’s game goes,” he said. Finally, Blanco played down the significance of Alaves’ narrow 2-1 defeat at the Bernabeu back in April. “Better not to look for references. We know they’re in great form. In the top flight any team can complicate your life. You have to give one hundred percent from everyone to try to bring back the three points,” he concluded.

top.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
top.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

top.description: Reunion day at The Hawthorns as Max O'Leary and Jed Wallace both prepare to face their former clubs [Shutterstock] West Bromwich Albion goalkeeper Max O'Leary has been in the form of his life this season, rescuing the Baggies on numerous occasions with some outstanding saves to keep them right in the heat of Championship promotion contention. But it is one save he actually failed to make that has dominated the build-up to Saturday's meeting with his boyhood club Bristol City at The Hawthorns. Bath-born O'Leary actually made his professional debut at The Hawthorns in a 2-2 FA Cup third-round tie between Albion and City back in January 2016 as a half-time substitute for injured visiting keeper Frank Fielding. And, when Albion scrambled in a 95th-minute equaliser to earn an Ashton Gate replay, which the Baggies went on to win, the scorer who left him on his knees in despair was none other than home midfielder James Morrison, now the Albion boss. "Yes, he managed to score against me in my first-ever game," O'Leary this week told BBC Radio Bristol's Sound of the City. "And he's mentioned it a few times since." Morrison confident Price will 'heal quickly' After 13 years on the books at Ashton Gate, during which he made 179 City appearances and had loan spells at Kidderminster Harriers, Bath City, Solihull Moors and Shrewsbury Town, he finally left 11 months ago to join Albion. And, ahead of his first meeting with City since, which also involves former Baggies skipper Jed Wallace potentially lining up against his old club, it has all gone rather nicely for O'Leary. "A lot of footballers just want to know where they stand," he added. "Ultimately i got that answer and moved on to a new challenge, which was the best thing for me - and it's worked out well so far." top.title: Sporting JAX defender earns second Scotland national team selection
top.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville Sporting Club Jacksonville defender Georgia Brown has earned a selection to the Scotland Women’s National Team for the upcoming FIFA Women’s World Cup second-round play-off matches against Sweden. The roster spot marks the second international call-up of the season for the 24-year-old defender, who competes professionally in the Gainbridge Super League. A victory over Sweden across the two-legged aggregate series would secure Scotland a place in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Qualification would mark only the second time in the national team’s history that it has reached the tournament. Brown was previously selected for Scotland’s qualifying matches against Czechia in October. Brown has started 11 Gainbridge Super League matches on the back line for Sporting JAX this season. She noted that representing her country offers a meaningful opportunity to compete for a World Cup spot. “It’s an incredible honor to represent Scotland; I’m extremely grateful every time I get to put the shirt on and the feeling of playing for something so much bigger than yourself is incredible,” Brown said. “And especially with the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup, that’s something every footballer dreams of, so it’s a really exciting time.” Brown explained that participating in national team camps contributes to her overall development on the pitch. She pointed to the daily standard of training with experienced teammates as an asset that sharpens her understanding before returning to club competition on the First Coast. “I feel like I gain something each time I go away with the squad,” Brown said. “The attention to detail and intensity of the sessions and games at camp helps raise my own level and improves my understanding of the game, which I try to show when I get back to Jacksonville. Just being surrounded by players who have lots of experience playing at the highest level allows me to learn so much about how they prepare for and approach games, especially during high-pressure moments.” Following the selection, JAX congratulated Brown on her call-up and wished her luck with the national team. top.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
top.description: Italy take on Fiji as the sides battle to avoid bottom spot – not that it could tempt many to attend the match - PA/Mike Egerton Italy ended their seven-match losing streak to edge Fiji 23-21, but the clash between the Nations Championship’s lowest ranked teams was watched by a sparse crowd at Allianz Stadium. Billed as the “Super Bowl of rugby”, finals weekend has struggled to attract interest with only 32,000 general admission tickets sold for day one, resulting in Twickenham’s top tier being closed. Acting as the curtain raiser to the fifth place play-off between Ireland and Australia later on Friday night, Fiji and Italy at least delivered a hard-fought battle that went down to the wire. Sumptuous second-half tries by Peniasi Dakuwaqa and Kitione Salawa propelled the Islanders into the lead, reeling in Italy who had established a 17-0 lead built on touch downs by Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera. Ultimately it was the boot of Tommaso Allan that proved the difference with the former Harlequins full-back landing a decisive 68th minute penalty to complete a 13-point individual haul. Fiji played some thrilling rugby in pursuit of a late victory but their execution was poor with a knock-on close to the line and wayward line-out throw important moments that cost them. Italy defended well and showed greater discipline to end a losing run that dated back to their historic victory over England in the penultimate round of the Six Nations. 06:45pm This weekend’s fixtures Today: Fiji 21 Italy 23 Ireland vs Australia 8.10pm Saturday: Wales vs Japan 1.10pm England vs New Zealand 4.40pm Sunday: Scotland vs Argentina 1.10pm South Africa vs France 4.40pm 06:43pm Man of the match Ross Vintcent “It was physical, full credit to Fiji. top.title: Xavier 71 – 83 Virginia: Just please make a shot
top.description: I’m assuming he’s pondering all those misses | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was hard to determine what was more infuriating today: the announcers, the officials, or Xavier’s steadfast refusal to make shots that matter. Virginia is an extremely good team, but Xavier made it a bit too easy for them today. For a game that tipped off absurdly early, this one turned into a decent contest once it got rolling. That took some time though, and by the time X had warmed to it, the Cavaliers had done what they needed to win. If you don’t believe me, ask the announcing crew that seemed to be Virginia grads (or possibly Chance Mallory’s uncles). With 12:12 to go in the first half, Mike Nwoko (15/4/1) was called for his second foul. I say called for, not committed, because it was a bad call. It functionally changed the game. Nwoko was too much for Virginia to handle when he was in, but he would get only 40 more seconds in the first half. Xavier ended that first half in a 15 point hole. Nwoko likely wouldn’t have scored 15 in the first half, but he would have made a difference. For the game his +/- was zero. X didn’t get the chance to find out if that would have held, because he had to watch. But Xavier also didn’t help themselves. They were hideous from the floor (39.3%), from behind the arc (1-8), and from the line (4-8) in the first half. That is appalling shooting and has been the story of the season so far. For the game the team was hardly any better, shooting .393/.227/.621. You can complain about the refereeing, which I found to be quite uneven, but you won’t win any games being that pitiful from deep or the line. Xavier is 332nd in the nation from the line. Had they made just four more, this game would have been different. That would have been 75%. Had they made two more three pointers, still a pitiful 32%, you could add six more points. That’s an easy, easy , ten points that Xavier left on the floor. Toss in 9-22 on layups and, well, you get it. Which is a shame, because they defended well enough to win. The Musketeers forced 21 turnovers and pressured the Cavaliers into missing six layups. Virginia ended up scoring 1.1 points per possession, but that came largely on good shooting from deep (12-30) and is still hardly an insurmountable number. It is insurmountable, though, if you leave easy points on the floor all game. Xavier’s defensive pressure was fun to watch, but when they couldn’t get out and run or at least create in transition, they couldn’t score. Ruben Dominguez is adding nothing to this team Dominguez is here for games like this. His whole raison d’etre is making three pointers. He hasn’t done that this season and he didn’t again today. He played nine minutes here today and played his second game where he made so little impact that he didn’t merit an offensive rating. Add in a 13 minute 0 offensive efficiency against Iowa and you have three games in which he has been so bad he’s been nothing. That means in 31 minutes over three games

nigeria.title: ECOWAS Speaker warns of levy shortfalls ahead of 2027 budget
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, Memounatou Ibrahima, has warned that rising public debt and mounting pressure on national finances could undermine member states’ ability to remit the Community Levy, urging governments to strengthen compliance ahead of the consideration of the regional body’s 2027 budget. Ibrahima gave the warning on Friday in Abuja during the opening of the 2026 Second Ordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament. She said the proposed 2027 budget was being considered at a time when member states were grappling with increasing demands for development financing and growing pressure on public finances. The Speaker urged national parliaments to intensify engagement with their respective governments to ensure regular collection and remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy. She also called on lawmakers to scrutinise budget proposals and ensure that public allocations addressed clearly identified needs and delivered measurable benefits to citizens across the region. She said: “One of the major highlights of our deliberations will be the consideration of the draft Community Budget for the 2027 financial year. “Indeed, persistent economic and financial constraints, characterised by mounting pressure on public finances and the indebtedness of our Member States, with the attendant risks to the remittance of the Community Levy, as well as increasing demands for development financing, require us to exercise particular vigilance and responsibility.” Ibrahima added: “I wish to urge our national parliaments to intensify their advocacy efforts with Member States at the appropriate political level to ensure the collection and systematic remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy.” She stressed that every budget allocation must be justified by its relevance and expected impact, while priority areas should be determined by efficiency, performance and tangible results for the people. The Speaker said the Parliament would also receive country reports and consider findings from oversight missions covering goods in transit, the ECOWAS Mission in The Gambia, regional agricultural projects and the development of a climate-friendly electricity market. She pledged to work with the new President of the ECOWAS Commission, Gen. Birame Diop, and other community institutions to advance regional integration. nigeria.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have activated a one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, keeping him at the club until 2028. According to the BBC, the option prevents overseas clubs from approaching the Portugal international over a pre-contract agreement when the transfer window opens on January 1. Fernandes’ previous contract was due to expire next summer. Fernandes, 32, and United are understood to have agreed to resume talks over a longer-term deal later, with their immediate focus on improving the club’s league position. The midfielder confirmed on Tuesday that contract discussions had been paused. United have been negotiating with Fernandes since the summer. He has turned down two offers, including the club’s initial proposal, but said the priority should be returning to winning ways. “I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games,” he said. Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 for £47m. He has since made 343 appearances, scoring 115 goals. Last season, he broke the Premier League assists record and won the individual player of the year awards as United finished third. United were open to selling him in the summer of 2025, when Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal made a substantial offer. After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes chose to stay, though he later said it “hurt” that the club had been willing to sell him. He lives and breathes football, is very analytical. He is already on the great managerial career already. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). sports.title: Cody Campbell once again makes it about himself
sports.description: Credit: Keith Inglis on X If there’s anybody who perfectly encapsulates the “get in there and make it about you” meme, it’s Texas Tech booster and oil tycoon Cody Campbell. Campbell has taken on outsized influence in not just investing millions in the Red Raiders athletic program to bring their teams to prominence, but throughout all of college football as well. He has been vocal in advocating for sweeping, transformational changes to the sport, particularly around the Protect College Sports Act and nationalizing television rights . But he has also rubbed others the wrong way with how he handles his business. He publicly clashed with former Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark with complaints over Friday night scheduling. And he’s shown himself to be a bit overly sensitive as he threatened a Lubbock radio station with pulling players from interviews over a critical tweet from a producer. He also regularly positions himself as part of the program through his appearances and messaging, acting as more of an owner or general manager than booster. So when Texas Tech clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance with a victory over TCU on Friday night, it was no surprise that Cody Campbell found a way to elbow himself into the spotlight. The booster showed up at the postgame press conference to ask a question to head coach Joey McGuire about the team having the momentum of a runaway freight train and why he’s so popular. Full exchange between Texas Tech mega-booster Cody Campbell and head coach Joey McGuire as he sat in on the postgame press conference following a win over TCU. Campbell’s question: “So, with all the adversity we dealt with over the last year, everything we’ve been through, can you talk about and I because I’ve seen it, the love that you have for your players, the love they have for you and and for each other, and how that’s gotten us through everything we’ve dealt with and why we’re in the place we’re in once again this year?” — Keith Inglis (@KeithInglisDT) November 27, 2026 Naturally, Cody Campbell will say that he’s only doing this because he wants McGuire and the team to get the respect and love that they are due and it’s all about lifting them up. But in reality, he’s only taking the attention for himself once again. There is no reason for him to be showing up and asking questions at a postgame press conference. None. But because he is the one that’s paying for all of this, he can do whatever he wants. If Campbell really wanted McGuire and the team to get some shine, the best thing he could do is get out of the way and let them actually have the moment for themselves. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The 2026 event had the following golfers competing for big-time money. 2026 Skins Game Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun The event, which took place at The Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida, returned to its original format of the event. The competition, which started back in 1983, abandoned the “reverse purse” from 2025, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Unlike 2025, where Xander Schauffele failed to win even a single skin during the event, this event was competitive till the very end. sports.description: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often? I am not a football manager or a football expert, and I don’t try to be, but I like to think I know a bit about football, having played the game myself for a number of years alongside being a huge football fan, watching many leagues and teams over the years, but most of all, of course, being a passionate Arsenal fan. Now, this may be controversial, but everyone is allowed an opinion, and I like to think, well, I hope, I know what I’m talking about sometimes. But what I would like to see is Mikel Arteta take the risk and sometimes play with two strikers up front. The rest of the formation and the way he decides to set up his team would not be a problem, but I’d genuinely like to see two up front. Why Not Play Havertz and Gyökeres Together? Now, I say this because, as we know, he seems to pick between either Kai Havertz or Viktor Gyökeres, and he rarely goes for the two of them together. But why not? If you haven’t tried it regularly, how do you know if it will work? Now, I don’t mean try it once and if it doesn’t work, give up. I mean give the two a chance to play together on a number of occasions! Everyone has their moans and groans when our strikers are not scoring, and yes, sometimes the delivery is not what it should be, but sometimes you have to take the game into your own hands and try, as we saw with Gyökeres’ goal against Borussia Dortmund the other night, which was a rather sweet strike. So why does Gyökeres seem to score left, right and centre for Sweden but struggle for Arsenal? There may be a number of reasons, but one reason I believe is because he is high in confidence, and more often than not, he is not playing as a lone striker as he tends to do for Arsenal. Sweden seems to have built their team around Gyökeres, and in the Nations League this year he has often played in a strike partnership, notably alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak, hence the great goalscoring form for his country. He scored six goals in five Nations League games this campaign and recently made history by scoring in eight consecutive matches in the competition , across two editions, scoring 12 goals during that run. Gyökeres is a player who can hold the ball up well and make that pass, whereas Havertz tends to struggle in that department depending on who is defending him. But he can offer good off-the-ball movement and good link-up play to the team. So why can the two not play together? (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) Could a Strike Partnership Bring More Goals? sports.title: Section 1 moving forward with plan to separate non-public schools during playoffs, despite state objections
sports.description: Section 1 is moving forward with a plan that would separate its public and non-public schools during postseason athletic competition, despite the move previously being overturned by a NYSPHSAA appeals panel. (Jim Franco/Times Union) When the Christian Brothers Academy football team takes the field Saturday night at Middletown High School for a Class AA state semifinal against Section 1's Mamaroneck, the Brothers will be doing so against a team from a section that is attempting to separate its public and non-public schools during postseason competition. A win Saturday in Middletown could also put CBA on a collision course for a state championship matchup next week against Syracuse's Christian Brothers Academy. If both CBA teams win their state semifinals this weekend, it would mark the second time in three years that the state title in New York's largest classification is contested between the two private schools that share the same name. First up for the Albany CBA squad is its matchup against Mamaroneck on Saturday at 6 p.m. The Tigers represent Section 1, which recently announced that despite objections from the New York State Public High School Athletic Association, it was moving forward with a planned change to its constitution that would separate private, parochial and charter schools from public schools during postseason athletic competition. That move would leave the non-public schools ineligible to participate in state playoffs. Section 1 announced the change to its constitution in June, following a 69-4 vote of member schools in the section, which includes Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Dutchess counties. Section 1's four non-public members - Albertus Magnus in Nanuet, Ursuline School in New Rochelle, Keio Academy in Purchase and The Lefell School in Hartsdale - were the only four institutions in the section to vote against the amendment. Three of the affected non-public schools filed an appeal with NYSPHSAA, and in July a three-person appeals panel from the state association ruled to overturn that amendment. However, at its October meeting, Section 1 announced plans to move forward with its plan beginning in the 2027-28 school year. In a statement to the Times Union, a Section 1 spokesperson said: "In June, 69 of the 73 schools that cast ballots supported proceeding with the changes, exceeding the two-thirds approval required for passage. Section One's decision to move forward with amendments to its constitution and bylaws is a matter of internal governance and reflects the direction of its member schools." The issue of private, parochial and charter schools - dubbed "schools without boundaries" by NYSPHSAA - competing against public institutions in state championship events has been a hot-button topic in recent years. sports.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville Sporting Club Jacksonville defender Georgia Brown has earned a selection to the Scotland Women’s National Team for the upcoming FIFA Women’s World Cup second-round play-off matches against Sweden. The roster spot marks the second international call-up of the season for the 24-year-old defender, who competes professionally in the Gainbridge Super League. A victory over Sweden across the two-legged aggregate series would secure Scotland a place in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Qualification would mark only the second time in the national team’s history that it has reached the tournament. Brown was previously selected for Scotland’s qualifying matches against Czechia in October. Brown has started 11 Gainbridge Super League matches on the back line for Sporting JAX this season. She noted that representing her country offers a meaningful opportunity to compete for a World Cup spot. “It’s an incredible honor to represent Scotland; I’m extremely grateful every time I get to put the shirt on and the feeling of playing for something so much bigger than yourself is incredible,” Brown said. “And especially with the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup, that’s something every footballer dreams of, so it’s a really exciting time.” Brown explained that participating in national team camps contributes to her overall development on the pitch. She pointed to the daily standard of training with experienced teammates as an asset that sharpens her understanding before returning to club competition on the First Coast. “I feel like I gain something each time I go away with the squad,” Brown said. “The attention to detail and intensity of the sessions and games at camp helps raise my own level and improves my understanding of the game, which I try to show when I get back to Jacksonville. sports.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
sports.description: Italy take on Fiji as the sides battle to avoid bottom spot – not that it could tempt many to attend the match - PA/Mike Egerton Italy ended their seven-match losing streak to edge Fiji 23-21, but the clash between the Nations Championship’s lowest ranked teams was watched by a sparse crowd at Allianz Stadium. Billed as the “Super Bowl of rugby”, finals weekend has struggled to attract interest with only 32,000 general admission tickets sold for day one, resulting in Twickenham’s top tier being closed. Acting as the curtain raiser to the fifth place play-off between Ireland and Australia later on Friday night, Fiji and Italy at least delivered a hard-fought battle that went down to the wire. Sumptuous second-half tries by Peniasi Dakuwaqa and Kitione Salawa propelled the Islanders into the lead, reeling in Italy who had established a 17-0 lead built on touch downs by Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera. Ultimately it was the boot of Tommaso Allan that proved the difference with the former Harlequins full-back landing a decisive 68th minute penalty to complete a 13-point individual haul. Fiji played some thrilling rugby in pursuit of a late victory but their execution was poor with a knock-on close to the line and wayward line-out throw important moments that cost them. Italy defended well and showed greater discipline to end a losing run that dated back to their historic victory over England in the penultimate round of the Six Nations. 06:45pm This weekend’s fixtures Today: Fiji 21 Italy 23 Ireland vs Australia 8.10pm Saturday: Wales vs Japan 1.10pm England vs New Zealand 4.40pm Sunday: Scotland vs Argentina 1.10pm South Africa vs France 4.40pm 06:43pm Man of the match Ross Vintcent “It was physical, full credit to Fiji. sports.title: Xavier 71 – 83 Virginia: Just please make a shot
sports.description: I’m assuming he’s pondering all those misses | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was hard to determine what was more infuriating today: the announcers, the officials, or Xavier’s steadfast refusal to make shots that matter. Virginia is an extremely good team, but Xavier made it a bit too easy for them today. For a game that tipped off absurdly early, this one turned into a decent contest once it got rolling. That took some time though, and by the time X had warmed to it, the Cavaliers had done what they needed to win. If you don’t believe me, ask the announcing crew that seemed to be Virginia grads (or possibly Chance Mallory’s uncles). With 12:12 to go in the first half, Mike Nwoko (15/4/1) was called for his second foul. I say called for, not committed, because it was a bad call. It functionally changed the game. Nwoko was too much for Virginia to handle when he was in, but he would get only 40 more seconds in the first half. Xavier ended that first half in a 15 point hole. Nwoko likely wouldn’t have scored 15 in the first half, but he would have made a difference. For the game his +/- was zero. X didn’t get the chance to find out if that would have held, because he had to watch. But Xavier also didn’t help themselves. They were hideous from the floor (39.3%), from behind the arc (1-8), and from the line (4-8) in the first half. That is appalling shooting and has been the story of the season so far. For the game the team was hardly any better, shooting .393/.227/.621. You can complain about the refereeing, which I found to be quite uneven, but you won’t win any games being that pitiful from deep or the line. Xavier is 332nd in the nation from the line. Had they made just four more, this game would have been different. That would have been 75%. Had they made two more three pointers, still a pitiful 32%, you could add six more points. That’s an easy, easy , ten points that Xavier left on the floor. Toss in 9-22 on layups and, well, you get it. Which is a shame, because they defended well enough to win. The Musketeers forced 21 turnovers and pressured the Cavaliers into missing six layups. Virginia ended up scoring 1.1 points per possession, but that came largely on good shooting from deep (12-30) and is still hardly an insurmountable number. It is insurmountable, though, if you leave easy points on the floor all game. Xavier’s defensive pressure was fun to watch, but when they couldn’t get out and run or at least create in transition, they couldn’t score. Ruben Dominguez is adding nothing to this team Dominguez is here for games like this. His whole raison d’etre is making three pointers. He hasn’t done that this season and he didn’t again today. He played nine minutes here today and played his second game where he made so little impact that he didn’t merit an offensive rating. Add in a 13 minute 0 offensive efficiency against Iowa and you have three games in which he has been so bad he’s been nothing. That means in 31 minutes over three games

technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. technology.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

science.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
science.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history?
